bugs.creator: michaelchirico4
bugs.summary: Qualifying base:: for OS-specific objects can produce R CMD check issues

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
I was working on https://github.com/r-lib/lintr/issues/3075 when this emerged:

```
pkg <- file.path(tempdir(), "ostest")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive=TRUE)

writeLines(
  c("Package: ostest",
    "Version: 0.1.0",
    "Title: T",
    "Description: D.",
    "License: GPL-2",
    "Imports: grDevices, utils"),
  file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
)
writeLines("export(f)", file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"))
writeLines(
  c("f <- function(cmd, file, from, to) {",
    "  if (.Platform$OS.type == 'windows') {",
    "    grDevices::win.metafile()",
    "    utils::winProgressBar()",
    "    base::shell(cmd)",
    "    base::shell.exec(file)",
    "    base::Sys.junction(from, to)",
    "  }",
    "}"),
  file.path(pkg, "R", "f.R")
)

print(tools:::.check_packages_used(dir=pkg))
```

Output on Linux

```
Missing or unexported objects:
  'base::shell' 'base::shell.exec' 'base::Sys.junction'
```

If we simply drop `base::` (e.g. plain `shell()`), there's no finding.

---

I also found `.fixupGFortranStd{err,out}` are omitted from `extras$base`, and that `utils::setInternet2()` is omitted from `.windows_only_proto_objects`, but I infer that those are intentional (the former, because it "should" be hidden and no package "should" be using them; the latter, because it's `.Defunct()`).
